newsitem.title: USA: Brazil soybean sale seen switched to U.S. origin.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean sale seen switched to U.S. origin.

text.p: Indications are that a cargo of soybeans sold by Brazil for August shipment was switched to U.S. origin, trade and U.S. export sources said.
"It was old crop. That is what I am hearing," one U.S. exporter said, adding that he did not know the destination.
"This is not public knowledge this sort of thing," he said, referring to the destination.
Trade sources did not know who had purchased the soybeans but there were rumors the vessel was headed for Europe.
The rumor boosted August soybean futures at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Several trade sources said the switch made sense because U.S. soybeans were priced competitively with Brazilian supplies for August shipment.
Export sources said U.S. soybeans for August shipment were quoted at $289.55 a tonne, FOB U.S. Gulf, identical to Brazilian FOB Paranagua bids.
They also pointed to reports that Brazil had overcommitted export sales and did not have enough soybeans available to meet August commitments.

Brazil had registered 8.39 million tonnes of soybeans for export as of July 15, according to Brazilian government figures released last week by the Brazilian Association of Vegetable Oils Industries. Soybean registrations were at 3.59 million tonnes by July 31, 1996.
"My concern has always been (whether) Brazil be able to meet August shipments when supplies got tighter," one oilseeds analyst said. "You can sell all you want but it comes down to can you ship it."
